So many people don't realize just how crazily amazing we have it. Yes, we're poor, can't afford to eat, live paycheque to paycheque, and are quite possibly in the process of watching some of the most corrupt activity on the world stage ever witnessed.

But on the other hand, we have for all intents and purposes the entirety of all human knowledge in the palm of our hands, man and machine are becoming more intertwined every day, the entire human genome has been mapped, the human brain is being mapped, the blind are seeing again, and countless hours of user-created entertainment freely exists for our consumption.

I think that 'recognition' problem is probably helped along a lot by greed. When you make things more efficient or better, you need to put money into R&D, which removes profit from your next quarter. As well, in becoming more efficient, you will need fewer employees, and will be laying people off. However, there is currently FAR more people of working age than there are positions which require a human operator, so many (I'd argue most) megacorporations are going to deliberately hold back progress and innovation, because then they would even sooner have to deal with the problem that the world is already severely suffering from, but world leaders refuse to acknowledge.

There's more people than there are jobs. That's just all there is to it. As more people get laid off, the entire economic system collapses, since there's fewer people with money to buy the larger number of products being produced, making less money for the corporations, who now have tons upon tons of unsold stock which are assumingly piling up somewhere, because the vast, VAST majority of people are all too goddamn poor to afford more and more and more random shit we can't eat, or use as shelter.

tl;dr: Recognition is indeed the problem, but what needs to be recognized is the state of the work force, not the products available.
